messages:
incidents-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT P1 — GPU pool us-west-2/g1 at 98% utilization, request queue growth and progressive 429s across hosted API. Autoscaler attempted scale-up but failed with provider quota errors. Marking as live.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Taking incident lead. Paging runtime and platform.
oncall-sre: samir @samir you able to join? can you confirm which pools are impacted and whether other regions are healthy?
samir: joining. quick check: g1 pool replicas all at 98-100%, avg queue length per node spiked from ~20 -> ~900 over last 7m.
samir: other regions (eu-central, ap-south) show normal patterns. this looks localized to us-west workload surge + failed scale.
engine-runtime: seeing repeated scaleup errors in the operator logs, provider returns 403/quotaExceeded on create VM.
engine-runtime: logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T03:12:01Z operator: scaleup request -> provider API error: QuotaExceeded: GPUs > allowed
2026-03-17T03:12:01Z autoscaler: aborting scale attempt, backoff=30s
```
eng-platform: provider quota windows just flashed a transient policy change earlier — looks like market-side quota reduced for our acct. I've opened a priority support ticket with cloud provider (TICKET-2031). ETA unknown.
elaine: customer-success here — customer flares already: two customers (tenant:alex-corp and tenant:edu-style) reported degraded responses and some timeouts. CS on triage with customers for impact details.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigations: (1) enable emergency fallback route to quantized model variant in us-west, (2) apply tenant-level shedding to heavy tenants, (3) temporarily increase cache TTLs to reduce backend calls.
runtime-pager: starting rollout of fallback model profile `redwood-small-q4` for us-west/g1. We'll route new requests to fallback and keep a small % to primary for validation. Applying now.
eng-platform: I can attempt a manual scale via spare AZ capacity (different quota). If operator create fails we can spin up pre-baked spare nodes in us-west-1 (cross-az). Need thumbs.
marta: ops-runner — I'll coordinate manual pool creation. prepping infra commands.
ops-runner: running:
```
# manual auth + create small nodepool
rcli provider create-nodepool --region us-west-2 --gpu-type a100 --count 3 --labels pool=evac
```
ops-runner: provider responded with partial success; 1/3 nodes failed with quota, 2/3 created. attaching to pool requires autoscaler update.
samir: updating pool routing to drop lowest-priority tenants onto the new evacuation pool.
elaine: CS: letting alex-corp know we are diverting some traffic to fallback model; they reported latency 2.3s -> 6-10s, some request failures. asking for business impact details.
runtime-pager: fallback rollout applied: 60% traffic -> redwood-small-q4, 40% -> primary. Observed 50% reduction in queue growth immediately.
oncall-sre: good. still seeing a residual queue but trending down. pressing cloud provider for quota increase is highest priority.
eng-platform: provider support responded: can increase GPU quota but requires account-level approval, ~2-3 hours. meanwhile suggest we expand capacity by moving some low-risk workloads to eu-central via routing policy.
samir: started tenant routing change for non-latency-sensitive tenants: shifting background batch tenants -> eu-central. Config change:
```
PATCH /routing/policy/us-west-2
- match: tenant in [batch-*]
- action: route -> eu-central-1
```
samir: change applied. batch tenant queue drained by 12% after 6m.
customer-success: confirming alex-corp reduced errors after fallback. they saw improved success rate but higher latency on some requests. we'll continue to monitor.
oncall-sre: summary of live mitigations done:
- fallback model rollout (redwood-small-q4) ✅
- manual spare nodes created (2/3) attached to evac pool ✅
- tenant shedding/rerouting for batch jobs -> eu-central ✅
- cache TTL increased on embedding routes ✅
- provider support ticket opened (TICKET-2031) — quota increase requested ⏳
engine-runtime: queue length now down 78% from peak. error 429s largely gone. marking incident as stabilizing.
elaine: CS will post customer impact notes in status page and email alex-corp & edu-style.
oncall-sre: moving to formal handoff in 10m to oncall followup. who will own postmortem?
elaine: I'll own customer-impact section.
eng-platform: I'll own infra/action items (quota gating, AZ fallback docs).
samir: I'll own runtime changes (fallback workflows, auto-shed heuristics).
runtime-pager: add immediate action item: add a hard guard in autoscaler to detect provider quota rejects and failover to pre-warmed evacuation pool automatically.
oncall-sre: agreed. add to action list.
ops-runner: created incident channel #inc-1715012345 for bridge notes and postmortem drafts.
oncall-sre: Estimated incident timeline for postmortem:
- T+0 (1715012345) alert
- Mitigations applied by T+15m
- Stabilized by T+35m
- Provider quota increase pending (external)
- Postmortem doc due in 48h, owners assigned.
marta: quick note — need runbook update for manual-create nodepool in quota-limited scenarios. adding to infra tickets.
eng-platform: I'll follow up with provider to request pre-approved burst quota for critical pools.
customer-success: customer impact: alex-corp reported 8% of requests failed during peak, edu-style had degraded throughput but no revenue impact reported. will compile final impact numbers.
oncall-sre: closing live phase. If anything regresses ping this thread. Thanks all for rapid response :thumbsup!
ops-runner: post-incident next steps:
- eng-platform -> (P1) request quota increase & pre-approval (owner: eng-platform)
- runtime -> (P1) autoscaler guard + automatic evac pool fallback (owner: samir)
- docs -> (P2) runbook for manual evacuation and cross-region routing (owner: marta)
- cs -> (P2) update status page and customer follow-up (owner: elaine)
- retro -> schedule 72h async postmortem with annotated timeline (owner: oncall-sre)
oncall-sre: closing thread for live ops. Will open postmortem doc in docs/incident-reports/ and link here. Good job everyone.
